why: Draws as many dashes as bounces left, instead of one more. Issue #688 names the zero-bounce shell -- the one the next wall stops -- as a state the cue must show; the 1-dash floor still keeps it visible, but a normal shell with one bounce left then reads exactly like it, and the three shipped starting budgets (normal 1, fast 0, ricochet 2) collapse to 1, 1, 2, so a fresh fast shell and a fresh normal one would carry the same mark.
killedBy: shell bounce-trail vocabulary (issue #688) draws one more dash than the bounces left, so a last-flight shell still has one
